newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegetable oil stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegetable oil stocks rise.

text.p: Pakistan's vegetable oil stocks rose amid higher imports ahead of the year-end holiday period, during which imports may be low while domestic prices may rise, dealers said on Saturday.
They said vessels were expected to arrive with a total cargo of 61,850 tonnes at Karachi between December 22 and 30.
But imports were likely to pick up early next month before the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan starting in mid-Januray.
Vegetable oil stocks rose to 136,000 tonnes in the week from 122,000 the previous week on higher imports and lower prices at Kuala Lumpur, a dealer at Saulat Enterprise said.
Stocks of RBD palm oil and olein rose to 115,000 tonnes, from 105,000 tonnes, while soybean and sunflower oil stocks were steady at 16,000 tonnes, the dealer said.
Palm oil and olein stocks with the state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan (GCP) rose to 5,000 tonnes from 1,000 a week ago.
GCP has booked imports of 10,500 tonnes of RBD palm oil and 4,000 tonnes of palm olein for shipment up to December 31.
One ship with 5,350 tonnes of soyoil and another with 28,000 tonnes of palm oil were expected to arrive at Karachi on December 25 and 22 respectively, dealers said.
Another ship with 25,000 tonnes palm oil was expected to arrive on December 28 and one with 3,500 tonnes of tallow on December 30.
